donor_source_ids: Simon 1962, 'The Architecture of Complexity' (Proc. Phil. Soc.)
donor_structure: hierarchy of near-decomposable subsystems: intrasubsystem interaction rates >> intersubsystem (ratio epsilon); short-run behavior approximately independent per subsystem, long-run aggregates; stable intermediate forms generate hierarchy
target_structure: H_t population -> metric on H ('nearby inheritance') -> R7 level object with cone boundaries
mapping: H_t inheritance links <-> intrablock couplings; inheritance cone <-> block boundary; level object <-> near-decomposable block; 'nearby inheritance' distance <-> interaction-rate ordering (rates as edge weights)
preserved_relations: hierarchy admits level-local analysis with bounded cross-level error O(epsilon)
rate separation gives a natural two-tier cost structure (cheap within, expensive between)
known_broken_relations: Simon gives RATE ORDERINGS, not a metric: no triangle-structured d on H follows; the R4 'what does nearby mean' question is only re-parameterized, not solved
no population/distribution content (R2) in Simon's framework
unknown_correspondences: whether cone boundaries in HSG (T06) coincide with Simon block boundaries under ecology drift
whether epsilon-uniformity across levels is checkable from H_t data
assumptions_added: interaction-rate ratio epsilon approximately uniform across levels
candidate_theorem: an inheritance hierarchy admits a cone-compatible metric d on H (d-cheap within blocks, d-expensive across) iff the inter/intra interaction-rate ratio is uniform across levels; otherwise only a quasimetric
proof_route: reduction of rate ordering to quasimetric via edge weights; metric-identification condition is the residual claim (not executed)
